title: The EU’s unfinished business in the Western Balkans – European Council on Foreign Relations
gist: Ahead of the European Commission's September 30th enlargement communication, Milica Delević argues the EU is taking the easy win — Montenegro and Albania, which have no difficult neighbours — while Kosovo, Bosnia and North Macedonia stay stuck, and that the original reconciliation purpose of Western Balkans enlargement is being lost to geopolitical expediency, leaving openings for Russia and China.

themes.theme: A dated decision point with a quick-wins bias

insights.claim: The European Commission is expected to unveil a comprehensive enlargement document on September 30th that will form the basis for European Council discussion in October and is likely to confirm Montenegro and Albania could finish negotiations soon.
insights.so_what: A firm, dated catalyst for EU enlargement policy and for accession-linked convergence trades in Montenegro and Albania.
insights.locator: On September 30th, the European Commission is expected
insights.speaker: Milica Delević

insights.claim: By focusing on Montenegro and Albania the EU has prioritised quick wins: both have demonstrated reform commitment but also have no major bilateral issues to resolve and no difficult neighbours to reconcile with.
insights.so_what: Warns that headline enlargement progress is selection bias, not proof the accession machinery works for harder cases.
insights.quote: Montenegro and Albania have demonstrated commitment to reform, but also have no major bilateral issues to resolve or difficult neighbours to reconcile with.
insights.locator: Any Western Balkan country that joins the EU after waiting over 20 years
insights.speaker: Milica Delević

insights.claim: Commission officials recently compared the annual cost of Montenegro's entry, per EU citizen, to the price of a cup of coffee — the framing being used to sell enlargement as a low-cost geopolitical gain.
insights.so_what: The cost framing that will shape the enlargement debate in the 2028-2034 EU budget negotiation; it only works for the smallest candidates.
insights.locator: Indeed, commission officials recently compared the annual cost
insights.speaker: Milica Delević

insights.claim: Two decades after the EU adopted its regional framework for the Western Balkans, only Croatia has become a fully fledged member state, with stagnation caused as much by internal EU blockages and lack of urgency as by regional governments' lack of commitment.
insights.so_what: The base rate for Western Balkans accession is one country in twenty years — a sobering prior against current optimism.
insights.locator: At the end of the wars of the 1990s
insights.speaker: Milica Delević

insights.claim: Ukraine and Moldova obtaining candidate status in 2022 revived member-state interest in the dormant Western Balkans process, which in turn prompted Montenegro and Albania to accelerate reforms.
insights.so_what: Western Balkans momentum is a derivative of the Ukraine war, so it is vulnerable to any shift in EU threat perception after a ceasefire.
insights.locator: After Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022
insights.speaker: Milica Delević

insights.claim: The driver of enlargement has changed fundamentally: Ukraine and Moldova's integration aims to strengthen European defences against a common threat, whereas Western Balkans enlargement was meant to foster regional stability and reconciliation between countries that had been at war with each other.
insights.so_what: Explains why current enlargement policy is structurally mismatched to the Balkan cases — a security rationale cannot substitute for a reconciliation one.
insights.locator: But the main impetus for this new momentum
insights.speaker: Milica Delević

insights.claim: Kosovo is stuck on unresolved status issues, Bosnia and Herzegovina carries a dysfunctional constitution imposed by the international community, and North Macedonia is held back by bilateral issues with EU neighbours — three blockages no enlargement communication can bypass.
insights.so_what: Names precisely which countries stay outside the accession trade, and why the blockage is structural rather than performance-related.
insights.locator: However, neither the EU nor the Western Balkans can ignore
insights.speaker: Milica Delević

insights.claim: Neglecting rule of law and democratic standards in favour of the broader geopolitical picture has diminished the accession process's transformative power and negatively impacted regional stability.
insights.so_what: The core causal claim: geopolitical leniency on conditionality destroys the leverage that makes accession work at all.
insights.locator: This is especially necessary for advancing the rule of law
insights.speaker: Milica Delević

themes.theme: Gradual integration and the influence vacuum

insights.claim: The Commission plans to present new proposals on gradual integration on September 30th, with a more ambitious and flexible framework aiming to include candidate countries in parts of the internal market as a reform incentive.
insights.so_what: Partial single-market access for non-members is the tradeable mechanism to watch — sectoral market opening ahead of formal accession.
insights.locator: It is planning to present new proposals on gradual integration
insights.speaker: Milica Delević

insights.claim: Reviving the Serbia-Kosovo dialogue, advancing Bosnian state reform and clearing member-state blockages on North Macedonia would advance Europe's geopolitical agenda by reducing opportunities for Russia, China and other actors to exert influence in the region.
insights.so_what: Frames unresolved bilateral disputes as the entry point for Russian and Chinese influence — the stalled cases are the geopolitical risk, not the accession ones.
insights.locator: In addition to exploring options for gradual integration
insights.speaker: Milica Delević

insights.claim: The presence of senior Serbian state representatives at the funeral of convicted Bosnian Serb war criminal Ratko Mladic caused shock and dismay across the region, within the EU and among many Serbian citizens — evidence of how unresolved the region's past remains.
insights.so_what: A concrete, recent signal that Serbian political alignment with EU norms is weaker than accession progress implies.
insights.locator: The recent funeral of convicted Bosnian Serb war criminal
insights.speaker: Milica Delević

insights.claim: If the EU does not close the remaining unresolved issues, its membership criteria will effectively reduce to the logic of an old Yugoslav comic line — that it is much better to be rich and beautiful than poor and ugly — amounting to the EU abandoning its own ambition and responsibility.
insights.so_what: The author's central judgement: selective enlargement would strip the process of its conditionality value, with knock-on effects for Ukraine and Moldova's paths too.
insights.quote: It is much better to be rich and beautiful than to be poor and ugly
insights.locator: The generations that lived through the good and the bad
insights.speaker: Milica Delević
